The word "adversarial" appears in the skill only at line 107 ("already adversarially reviewed", describing Stage 10/12), line 114 (same, referring back), and line 118 (the optional pass).
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED. The claim asserts the whole clause restates the skill's scoping rule, but the load-bearing half survives scrutiny. The scoping half ("scoped only to the delta ship itself just generated") does duplicate lines 107/109/114. However the skill calls the *adversarial* review optional and gates it on operator judgment the skill cannot make — line 118, "Optionally ... for large or risky changes". The skill's own mandatory Step 6 pass (line 109) is a Correctness/Security/Performance/Hygiene checklist and is never labelled adversarial. So KICKOFF's unconditional "adversarial pre-landing review" elects a mode the skill offers but leaves off by default; under the classification rubric that is mode selection / emphasis of something the skill makes optional, which is load-bearing, severity low. Deleting this clause would change behavior (the adversarial pass would be skipped on a not-obviously-risky milestone), which a pure restatement cannot do. The severity is low because the scoping words riding alongside it are genuinely redundant and could be trimmed to just "run the optional adversarial pass".

verdicts.evidence: ABSENCE VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY. The skill is a single 218-line file with no `references/` chain (`find .../skills/ship -type f` returns only SKILL.md). `grep -inE "land-and-deploy|land |landing|do not merge|don'?t merge|never merge|deploy|hand off|handoff|stop there|terminate|boundary|after the PR|post-PR"` over the whole file returns only: line 48 (release/publish CI workflow detection — "not a web service with existing deployment", unrelated), line 84 ("Empty/zero/**boundary** states" — test coverage, unrelated), line 103 ("## Step 6: Pre-landing review"), line 125 ("what kind of release this is"), line 136 ("never landed on the base branch" — CHANGELOG collapsing), line 191 ("## Pre-Landing Review" PR body heading). No hit forbids merging or deploying. The nearest terminal statement is SKILL.md:207 "**Output the PR/MR URL.**", and it is preceded five lines earlier by SKILL.md:172 "**You are NOT done** — PR creation is a mandatory final step." The `land-and-deploy` skill exists at `/home/ubuntu/skillsproject/dev-kit/plugins/dev-kit-core/skills/land-and-deploy` and `ship` never names it.
verdicts.reasoning: CONFIRMED after hunting: I re-ran the absence check myself across merge/deploy/land/handoff/terminate/boundary vocabulary plus synonyms, and confirmed the skill has no `references/` directory to hide the rule in. Two independent grounds make the KICKOFF sentence load-bearing and require KEEPING it. (1) Absence: the skill states where it ends but never forbids going further — an implicit terminus is not a prohibition, and it sits next to line 172's opposite-direction "You are NOT done" plus line 8's "DO IT / run straight through" framing, which an over-eager agent can over-read into merging the PR it was just told to create. (2) Cross-skill sequencing: "land-and-deploy is a separate skill that runs after step 14" is pipeline-position information — the skill cannot know a step 14 exists or that document-release must run against an open PR before landing. That is ordering across skills, which is load-bearing on its own terms. Medium severity: the finding is on the SKILL — `ship` should encode its own terminal boundary and name the handoff — while the guide text must be retained until it does.
